title: Minimum Cost to Connect All Cities
statement: You are given an integer n and a list roads, where the cities are labeled 1 to n and each road is a triple [a, b, cost] meaning a bidirectional road can be built between city a and city b for the given cost. You want every city to be reachable from every other city, directly or indirectly. Return the minimum total cost to achieve this, or -1 if it is impossible with the roads provided. Duplicate roads may connect the same pair of cities with different costs; you may build any subset of roads, so only the cheapest option between a pair ever matters. When n is 1 the cities are already all connected and the answer is 0.
hints: You want the cheapest set of roads that ties every city into one connected group. Think greedily: sort the candidate roads from cheapest to most expensive and add a road only when it joins two cities that are not already reachable from each other. What you need is a fast way to test 'are these two cities already linked?'

Sort the roads by ascending cost and walk them once, using union-find: a road is worth building only when its two endpoints are in different components, so union() returning False means skip it (and its cost).

Add a road's cost only when union succeeds, and count those successful merges. A tree over n cities needs exactly n-1 merges; if you finish with fewer, some cities were never joined, so return -1. Cheaper duplicate edges are handled automatically because sorting reaches the cheap one first.
